title: Rankless Rally
user: Puzzle players who enjoy improving a score but do not want a grindy ranked ladder, account requirement, or a daily puzzle that disappears forever.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A creator reports that a simple daily leaderboard caused active players to replay logic puzzles to improve rank more than progression did, despite no rewards or sharing incentives.
A post about enclose.horse praises a one-a-day spatial puzzle that also permits the whole archive and user-made levels, rather than locking play behind a single daily board.

recurrence: One source observes score-driven replay directly; the other highlights that a daily format can coexist with an accessible archive and creation.
current_workaround: Replay the daily until it is optimized, keep screenshots of old scores, or move to a competitive game with a full ranking system.
incumbents_and_gap: Daily leaderboards and Puzzmo-style archives exist, but standard rank tables intensify competition. Casual players lack a compact score game that celebrates personal improvement and lets a host share a replay without an account.
smallest_useful_product: A 90-second spatial-routing puzzle with one daily board and a permanent archive. Each board awards a three-part 'rally card'—speed, elegance, and rescue count—so players can improve different dimensions; a replay ghost shows only a chosen friend’s path via a room code. Inputs are mouse/touch/keyboard. Non-goals: global MMR, chat, streak loss, algorithmic feed, and user-generated content moderation in v1.
success_measure: At least 25% of completed boards are replayed once and at least 15% of players open a shared replay ghost without creating an account.
monetization: free — the score card and archive must remain shareable; a one-time theme pack can support hosting without selling retries.
constraints: Anti-cheat should verify deterministic move logs server-side; do not expose personal profiles by default; provide color-blind-safe route symbols.
why_distinct: It treats improvement as several interpretable personal goals, not as an engagement ladder or a clone of an existing daily puzzle.
